s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules with a symmetric distribution on the trunk and extremities
salient_findings: red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
elevated eosinophil count and tryptase level
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
lesions were symmetrically distributed and did not coalesce
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes were unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL)
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease with eosinophilia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tryptase and eosinophilia, consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes, consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tryptase and skin lesions, consistent with mastocytosis

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated eosinophils and skin lesions, consistent with eosinophilic granuloma

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Eosinophilia and skin lesions, consistent with Churg-Strauss syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and elevated vitamin B12 levels are consistent with mastocytosis. The skin biopsy showing nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils and the bone marrow analysis showing hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease with eosinophilia
rejected.why: Erdheim-Chester disease typically presents with multisystem involvement, including bone, cardiovascular, and central nervous system, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presents with CD1a positive cells on immunohistochemistry, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic granuloma is a type of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and typically presents with solitary bone lesions, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: Churg-Strauss syndrome typically presents with asthma, eosinophilia, and vasculitis, which is not seen in this patient
